title: Bass instruments of the era: string bass, banjo and tuba
summary: They discuss how white rhythm sections used piano, bass and drums rather than banjo or brass bass, and that Chink Martin sometimes played tuba on records with Sharky.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: No, string bass. Did you hear any banjos or brass basses in those days?

No, they didn't seem to be in style in those days. It was a piano bass drums rhythm section. That was the fad. Now black bands used banjo players. I believe Papa Celestan, Papa Celestan's band played for my senior prom. And he had a banjo in his band. But it was a string bass too. It wasn't a tuba.

The only brass bass player that I can think of that was playing inside then in those days was a guy called Lefty Ironman, who played with Buck Banville at the Plum Plant, the American Legion Dance Hall. That may have been a place you didn't go to.
Now Cink Martin played an iron bass on occasion. He was a good bass player too. Good tuba player. Cink Martin. But not often.
I mean I just didn't hear him do it.
He did a few records. Yeah.
But I mean that's just, I don't remember, when you say it was Sharky in person I don't remember him playing anything but string bass. No I don't either.
But he did a couple of records with Sharky, Over the Waves and things like that, that he played tuba on. He played really good.
